questions.title: Alternate Playlist Shuffle
questions.description:
A DJ shuffles two playlists strictly alternately (track from list A, track from list B, ...); when one list runs out, the leftovers of the other are appended. The zip builtin is banned.

Implement only this function:

    def interleave(a, b):

It must return the shuffled list. The harness prints the result space-separated.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.
Line 3: m.
Line 4: m space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the interleaved list, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n, m <= 1000, -1000 <= value <= 1000
questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def interleave(a, b):
    out = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(a) or i < len(b):
        if i < len(a):
            out.append(a[i])
        if i < len(b):
            out.append(b[i])
        i += 1
    return out


data = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(data[0])
a = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
m = int(data[1 + n])
b = list(map(int, data[2 + n:2 + n + m]))
print(" ".join(map(str, interleave(a, b))))

questions.title: Remove Duplicates Keep Order
questions.description:
Keep only the first occurrence of each value while preserving the original order.

Implement only this function:

    def dedupe(lst):

It must return a list of the distinct values in first-occurrence order. The harness prints the result space-separated.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the deduplicated list, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1000 <= value <= 1000
questions.sourcecode:
import sys

def dedupe(lst):
    seen = set()
    out = []
    for v in lst:
        if v not in seen:
            seen.add(v)
            out.append(v)
    return out

data = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(data[0])
lst = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
print(" ".join(map(str, dedupe(lst))))

questions.title: Rotate the Roster by K
questions.description:
A duty roster rotates right by k slots: the last k elements move to the front. k may be larger than the roster length — reduce it with modulo first.

Implement only this function:

    def rotate_list(lst, k):

It must return the list rotated right by k (use k % n; slicing is expected). The harness prints the result space-separated.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.
Line 3: k.

Output Format:
One line with the rotated list, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 0 <= k <= 1000000
questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def rotate_list(lst, k):
    n = len(lst)
    k = k % n
    return lst[n - k:] + lst[:n - k]

questions.title: Silver Time Without Sorting
questions.description:
Race times arrive one by one; the board must NOT be rearranged, yet the silver (second-smallest distinct) time is needed. Track it with running variables only.

Implement only this function:

    def silver_time(times):

It must return the second smallest distinct value using a single scan with best/second variables (no sorting helpers). The input always has at least two distinct values.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n space-separated times.

Output Format:
One line with the silver time.

Constraints:
2 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= time <= 10000
questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def silver_time(times):
    best = None
    second = None
    for t in times:
        if best is None or t < best:
            second = best
            best = t
        elif t != best and (second is None or t < second):
            second = t
    return second


data = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(data[0])
times = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
print(silver_time(times))

def slot_in(lst, val):
    i = 0
    while i < len(lst) and lst[i] < val:
        i += 1
    return lst[:i] + [val] + lst[i:]

questions.title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
questions.description:
Two courier routes are each sorted by delivery time; merge them into one sorted route with the classic two-pointer walk (no sorting helpers).

Implement only this function:

    def merge_two_lists(a, b):

It must return one ascending list containing all values of a and b, merged by advancing two indices. The harness prints the result space-separated.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n space-separated integers (ascending).
Line 3: m.
Line 4: m space-separated integers (ascending).

Output Format:
One line with the merged list, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n, m <= 1000, -1000 <= value <= 1000
questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def merge_two_lists(a, b):
    out = []
    i = 0
    j = 0
    while i < len(a) and j < len(b):
        if a[i] <= b[j]:
            out.append(a[i])
            i += 1
        else:
            out.append(b[j])
            j += 1
    while i < len(a):
        out.append(a[i])
        i += 1
    while j < len(b):
        out.append(b[j])
        j += 1
    return out


data = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(data[0])
a = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
m = int(data[1 + n])
b = list(map(int, data[2 + n:2 + n + m]))
print(" ".join(map(str, merge_two_lists(a, b))))

questions.title: Conveyor Window Peak
questions.description:
A conveyor belt reports belt-heat readings; the control system watches the hottest window of exactly k consecutive readings. Compute it with a sliding window in one pass (no sum() and no sorting helpers).

Implement only this function:

    def peak_window(lst, k):

It must return the maximum sum of k consecutive elements — build the first window manually, then slide by adding the entering element and subtracting the leaving one.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.
Line 3: k (1 <= k <= n).

Output Format:
One line with the maximum window sum.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= k <= n, -1000 <= value <= 1000
questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def peak_window(lst, k):
    cur = 0
    for i in range(k):
        cur += lst[i]
    best = cur
    for i in range(k, len(lst)):
        cur += lst[i] - lst[i - k]
        if cur > best:
            best = cur
    return best


data = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(data[0])
lst = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
k = int(data[1 + n])
print(peak_window(lst, k))

questions.title: Carousel Seat Remap
questions.description:
A carousel remaps riders to seats by pure index arithmetic: the rider at index i moves to seat (i + k) % n. Slicing syntax is banned — build the new list with the modulo remapping only.

Implement only this function:

    def rotate_remap(lst, k):

It must create a result list of n placeholders and assign result[(i + k) % n] = lst[i] for every i (equivalent to rotating right by k % n).

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.
Line 3: k.

Output Format:
One line with the remapped seats, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 0 <= k <= 1000000
questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def rotate_remap(lst, k):
    n = len(lst)
    out = [0] * n
    for i in range(n):
        out[(i + k) % n] = lst[i]
    return out


data = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(data[0])
lst = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
k = int(data[1 + n])
print(" ".join(map(str, rotate_remap(lst, k))))
